title: What is Tailwind CSS?
definition: A utility-first CSS framework packed with classes like flex, pt-4, text-center and rotate-90 that can be composed to build any design, directly in your markup.
simpleExplanation: Instead of writing custom CSS rules in a separate file (like `.my-button { padding: 10px; color: red; }`), Tailwind gives you thousands of tiny, pre-made CSS classes. You just slap them directly onto your HTML elements: `<button class="p-2 text-red-500">`.
realWorldExample: Building a card component in 2 minutes without ever leaving your HTML/JSX file, and without having to invent class names like `card-container-outer-wrapper`.

basic: Is Tailwind a UI Kit like Bootstrap (which provides pre-made buttons and navbars)?
intermediate: How does Tailwind handle massive CSS file sizes in production?

answers.question: Like Bootstrap?
answers.answer: No. Bootstrap gives you pre-designed components (`btn btn-primary`). Tailwind gives you raw building blocks (`bg-blue-500 px-4 py-2 rounded`). You design your own components.

answers.question: File sizes?
answers.answer: Tailwind automatically scans your HTML/JS files, detects exactly which classes you actually used, and completely deletes all the unused classes. The final production CSS file is usually less than 10kb.
